title: The user-visible name is Cairnfield
acceptance: CFBundleDisplayName is Cairnfield in the app and the share extension, so the home screen and App Store show Cairnfield
PRODUCT_NAME, the three bundle identifiers, the app group, the CloudKit container, directory names and Swift symbols all remain Cairn and are untouched
User-visible copy says Cairnfield — the sidebar title, library empty states, and the share extension's confirmation
README and ROADMAP call the app Cairnfield while noting the code and bundle stay Cairn
invariants.sh X7 passes WITHOUT the ALLOW_IDENTITY_CHANGE waiver, proving no identifier moved
notes: Stacks, Cairn and Pilcrow were all unavailable at App Store Connect reservation despite looking free in store search. Cairnfield is a real archaeological term — a landscape scattered with many cairns — which is a better fit for an archive than a single marker. The display name is deliberately decoupled from the bundle id and repo, which stay Cairn: mismatched bundle ids and display names are entirely normal and nobody but the developer sees the identifier. Criterion 5 is the safety property — if X7 fails without the waiver, the task has changed an identifier it should not have.
